claim_decisions.statement: Source dated 2024-05-08 reports: The 2023/2024 season’s late onset, dry spells and heat affected crops and livestock; over nine million people in 84 of 117 districts were affected, with Central, Eastern, Southern and Western provinces hardest hit.

claim_decisions.reason: An anticipated protection-risk statement scoped to the 2024 drought appeal; no subsequent incidence or persistence was verified, so it is not loaded as a live projected finding.

claim_decisions.statement: Source dated 2025-12 reports: The 2023/2024 drought affected over nine million people in more than 70% of 117 districts; over three million children were food insecure and more than 51,000 faced severe-wasting risk.

claim_decisions.reason: Retain bounded source-supported finding with vintage and causal limitations; no extrapolation to 2026 or evaluated impact.
claim_decisions.statement: Source dated 2025-12 reports: In 2025, UNICEF rehabilitated 86 boreholes (34 at health facilities) in drought-affected districts, benefiting 21,500; a separate cholera response restored water to 4,108 through seven boreholes.

claim_decisions.reason: Retain bounded source-supported finding with vintage and causal limitations; no extrapolation to 2026 or evaluated impact.
claim_decisions.statement: UNICEF reports drought cash delivery through the Social Cash Transfer system, with aggregate reach including regular and emergency households; reported avoided asset sales are not an independently evaluated effect.
claim_decisions.uncertainty: The 2.2 million aggregate is not retained as a distinct new drought-beneficiary total, because regular and emergency coverage overlap in programme reporting.

claim_decisions.statement: Source dated 2025-09 reports: Among 950 surveyed assistance recipients, 66.7% said aid met household priorities; 27.3% disagreed, citing unmet needs, exclusion or access barriers.

claim_decisions.statement: The recipient survey reports different protection-service perceptions in Lunga and Gwembe and identifies remoteness, roads and communications as constraints.
claim_decisions.uncertainty: Seven-versus-eight district discrepancy and variable denominators remain unresolved; percentages are omitted and this is not a district-risk ranking.

claim_decisions.statement: Source dated 2025-09 reports: Among respondents, 42.3% felt excluded from decisions and 12.4% reported discrimination or access barriers; 87% reported no barriers.
claim_decisions.uncertainty: Recipient perceptions only, with unclear district coverage; not general-population discrimination prevalence or a causal drought effect.

claim_decisions.statement: Source dated 2026-03-20 reports: FAO reports that drought-damaged crops, dried water sources and livestock losses persisted in Gwembe and Sinazongwe after above-average 2025/2026 rains supported crop recovery; some households entered later seasons with depleted herds and assets.

claim_decisions.statement: Source dated 2026-03-20 reports: FAO and partners distributed 1,312 goats to vulnerable farmers in Gwembe and Sinazongwe, reporting about 1,600 people reached, a majority women; support also included animal husbandry, disease-control and climate-smart agriculture training.

claim_decisions.statement: Source dated 2026-03-20 reports: A woman farmer from Luumbo Camp, Munyumbwe, told FAO she had lost livestock in the drought and received replacement goats; the project says a pass-on arrangement is intended to extend offspring to other households.

claim_decisions.statement: Source dated 2026-01-30 reports: Late-December 2025 floods in Lundazi and Lumezi submerged Lundazi’s treatment plant, leaving over 40,000 people without safe water; UNICEF describes child displacement, missed school, crop losses and greater illness risk.

claim_decisions.reason: Retain bounded source-supported finding with vintage and causal limitations; no extrapolation to 2026 or evaluated impact.
claim_decisions.statement: Source dated 2026-01-30 reports: UNICEF reported orienting over 75 community volunteers across four flood-affected health facilities and 11 additional facilities remotely; three hand pumps were provided for installation and three clinic boreholes remained planned.

gaps: The expired appeal's prospective protection risks are not treated as verified incidents; the recipient survey supports limited protection/access context with unresolved coverage discrepancy.

executive_assessment.text: Gwembe/Sinazongwe drought recovery and Lundazi/Lumezi flood-water disruption illustrate different local livelihoods and service vulnerabilities.
Cash and borehole outputs are reported activities; recipient perceptions identify inclusion/access concerns but do not establish causal effects or representative district comparisons.
